newsitem.title: HUNGARY: RWE's Budapest unit posts HUF 3bln '96 loss.
newsitem.headline: RWE's Budapest unit posts HUF 3bln '96 loss.

text.p: Budapest's electricity distributor Elmu Rt, which is controlled by Germany's RWE and EVS, posted a loss of 3.04 billion forints in 1996, caused in part by October's cancelled energy price rises,

The losses by the company, in which RWE and EVS bought a joint 46.15 percent stake at the end of 1995, was up from 0.81 billion forints in 1995, but down from 3.77 billion forints in 1994, the Hungarian daily Vilaggazdasag said on Friday referring to Elmu as a source.

Some 1.3 billion forint of the 1996 loss was caused by the delay in energy price hikes, which the government originally planned for October 1996, but only introduced on January 1 this year, the paper said, ading that the remaining part of the loss was due to financing consumers' unpaid bills.
ELMU expects to post a profit this year, the amount of which will depend on energy price hikes to be introduced through the new system of quarterly price adjustments, the paper said.
